o.norm: a bit of a back door in!

checks expected order, and the + indicates that element had a next sibling at time of emission note that we don't get a full doc, just the fragment (and the context at the end of the stack) as read to completion

i.norm: Verifies that {@link StreamParser} can parse an HTML fragment and emit its elements, in document order, via {@link StreamParser#stream()}.

Appends a compact, human-readable signature of {@code element} to {@code summary}, capturing the details this test asserts on:
  • the tag name,
  • {@code #id} when the element has an {@code id} attribute,
  • {@code [text]} when the element has its own text,
  • a trailing {@code +} when the element had a next sibling at the moment it was emitted.
Each signature is terminated with a {@code ;}.
Returns true once the parser has read its input to completion and released the underlying reader. Reaches through the parser internals as a back door, since there is no public "is closed" API.

Elements are emitted in document order; children come before their parents. The trailing '+' marks elements that already had a next sibling when emitted. Note we only get the fragment plus the context element at the end of the stack, not a full document.
Streaming to completion closes the parser and releases the reader.
